body:
_Migrated from issue #1237, filed 2026-07-29._

A translator opens a PR updating one locale's `messages.po`. CI goes green. Then main picks up an automated `Update translations [skip ci]` commit and the PR flips to CONFLICTING, with no `msgid` or `msgstr` text in conflict — so the translator can't fix it by translating anything, and someone here has to re-author the contribution by hand before it can land.

`scripts/freeze_pot_creation_date.py` already removed one instance of this: `POT-Creation-Date` (bot-touched) sits on the line directly above `PO-Revision-Date` (translator-touched), git can't split adjacent changed lines into separate hunks, so the header pair conflicted on its own. That note measured PR #938 and concluded the `#:` source-location churn in the same file merged cleanly, "unchanged msgid lines separate those hunks."

That holds for a PR that only fills in empty `msgstr`s. It does not hold for a PR that removes a `#, fuzzy` flag, because the flag sits *between* the `#:` line and the `msgid`:

```
#: cps/admin.py:610      <- bot rewrites this when any line number shifts
#, fuzzy                 <- translator deletes this when confirming a real translation
msgid "Hardcover token expires"
```

There is no unchanged line between them, so it's the same failure as the header pair, one field pair over. #1227 hit exactly this: 11 conflict hunks, every one a `#:` ref plus the `#, fuzzy` flag under it, zero conflicts in translation text. The `#:` churn came from an unrelated code change shifting line numbers in `cps/admin.py`.

This is the most common shape a good translation contribution takes — confirming entries that gettext had guessed and left provisional. #1227 removed 57 of them. So the conflict is likelier on the more valuable PRs, and it fires on any code change anywhere near a translated string, which is most of them.

**Direction, not yet decided:** the bot's `msgmerge` in `scripts/update_translations.sh` could write locale `.po` files with `--no-location`, keeping `#:` refs in `messages.pot` (where translators and tooling actually read them) and out of the 28 locale catalogs that get rewritten on every push. That would need checking against whatever translator tooling relies on refs being present per-locale — Weblate and Poedit both read them for context — plus a one-time churn commit stripping locations from all 28 files, so it wants a decision before anyone implements it. Freezing the refs the way the creation date is frozen isn't equivalent: unlike the date, refs do carry information.

Until then, adopting one of these by hand costs a `msgcat --use-first <pr> <main>` followed by `msgmerge --no-fuzzy-matching` against the committed POT, which reconciles by content instead of hand-patching the comment churn — see #1236 for the worked example.
title: Community translation PRs still go CONFLICTING when they remove a fuzzy flag
